title: GOV-0002: composed-tree verification is implicit, not a named merge gate
problem:
## Observed
On a `pull_request` event, `actions/checkout` checks out `refs/pull/N/merge` — GitHub's own composition of head onto base — so CI step 5 already runs on a composed tree. But nothing **asserts** that, **records** the composed tree hash, or **names** the property. `BRANCH_GREEN ≠ MERGE_SAFE` is enforced by accident of checkout behaviour, not by a gate. There is no `badf/composed-tree` status check.

## Expected (GITHUB_CONTROL_PLANE.md §7 of the adopted doctrine)
An explicit, named, required status check that computes `source_head_sha + current_target_sha + merge_method → expected_result_tree`, records the tree hash as evidence, and fails when the composition cannot be reproduced. `MERGE_ELIGIBLE` only after it passes against the **current** base.

## Evidence
`grep -n composed .github/workflows/badf-gates.yml` → comments only. WP-0010's G08 dossier records a composed-tree artifact (tree `e40c93f`) — the property is proven at dossier level for one WP, never as a merge gate.

## Unknowns
Whether a single `governance` job should stay monolithic or split into `badf/composed-tree`, `badf/tests`, `badf/traceability` so the decision surface is observable (§8 of the doctrine). Splitting changes the ruleset's required contexts; that is a governance edit.

## Proposed work package
`BADF-WP-0017` — record `refs/pull/N/merge` tree hash as a CI artifact; assert it equals `git merge-tree`(base, head) recomputed in-job; expose as its own step. Splitting the job is a follow-on decision.
